title: Sakura Sakura
origin: Edo-period urban melody, standardised as a beginner koto piece in the Meiji era

pd.detail: Anonymous Edo-period melody known as 'Saita Sakura', printed for koto students in the Tokyo Academy of Music collection Sokyoku Shu (1888).
pd.sourceEdition: Public-domain reference notation of the standard Meiji setting: melody line in A, pitch set A B C E F, 14 bars in seven two-bar phrases
pd.notes: Melody only, no lyrics. The tune sits in one octave above the tonic - A B C for the opening phrase and the upper E F for the 'miwatasu kagiri' phrase - and cadences on the tonic A, which is how the 14 bars are grouped here as head (6) + verse (4) + coda (4). The chords are a light modal harmonisation, not part of the unaccompanied koto original.

pd.detail: Anonymous Japanese text, no identifiable author, attested in print with this koto melody in the Tokyo Academy of Music's Sokyoku Shu (1888); the tune itself circulated in the late Edo period as 'Saita Sakura' under a different text.
pd.sourceEdition: Sokyoku Shu (Collection of Japanese Koto Music), Tokyo Academy of Music, 1888 - the original Meiji verse, romanized

lyrics.notes: The single 1888 verse is the only text carried. The verse added in 1941 by the Japanese Ministry of Education - which most modern singers know as the first verse - is a 20th-century text with no pre-1930 basis and is omitted. Lines 1-3 of the 1888 verse sit here, one line per two bars.
